end point, a BIRC performed a central assessment of PFS in a randomly selected
subgroup of patients. Secondary end points included overall survival (OS),
overall response rate (ORR), clinical benefit rate, and safety and tolerability.
Statistical Analysis
The primary analysis compared PFS between the treatment arms using
a stratified log-rank test. The treatment effect was estimated using a Cox
proportional hazards model overall and in relevant subgroups. The central PFS

performed after observing approximately 364 local PFS events to detect a hazard

The treatment effect was estimated using a Cox proportional hazards model overall and in relevant subgroups. The primary PFS analysis was to be performed after observing approximately 364 local PFS events to detect a hazard ratio of 0.67 with 95% power and a one-sided 2.5% level of significance. OS was compared between the treatment groups using a stratified log- rank test at a one-sided 2.5% level if the primary PFS end point was significant. 27|fulvestrant. The primary end point was locally assessed progression-free survival. Secondary end
28|points included overall survival, overall response rate, and safety.
29|Results
30|A total of 484 postmenopausal women were randomly assigned to ribociclib plus fulvestrant, and
31|242 were assigned to placebo plus fulvestrant. Median progression-free survival was significantly
32|improved with ribociclib plus fulvestrant versus placebo plus fulvestrant: 20.5 months (95% CI,
33|18.5 to 23.5 months) versus 12.8 months (95% CI, 10.9 to 16.3 months), respectively (hazard
34|ratio, 0.593; 95% CI, 0.480 to 0.732; P , .001). Consistent treatment effects were observed in
35|patients who were treatment na ̈ıve in the advanced setting (hazard ratio, 0.577; 95% CI, 0.415 to
36|0.802), as well as in patients who had received up to one line of prior endocrine therapy for
37|advanced disease (hazard ratio, 0.565; 95% CI, 0.428 to 0.744). Among patients with measurable
38|disease, the overall response rate was 40.9% for the ribociclib plus fulvestrant arm and 28.7% for
39|placebo plus fulvestrant. Grade 3 adverse events reported in $ 10% of patients in either arm
40|(ribociclib plus fulvestrant v placebo plus fulvestrant) were neutropenia (46.6% v 0%) and leu-
41|kopenia (13.5% v 0%); the only grade 4 event reported in $ 5% of patients was neutropenia
42|(6.8% v 0%).
43|Conclusion
44|Ribociclib plus fulvestrant might represent a new first- or second-line treatment option in hormone
45|receptor-positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative advanced breast cancer.

The remaining death in the placebo 4|plus fulvestrant arm resulted from a pulmonary embolism. 5|DISCUSSION 6|The MONALEESA-3 study demonstrated that ribociclib plus 7|fulvestrant significantly improves PFS compared with fulvestrant 8|alone in postmenopausal women with HR-positive/HER2-negative 9|advanced breast cancer, resulting in a 41% reduction in the risk of 10|progression. To our knowledge, MONALEESA-3 is the first study 11|to evaluate a CDK4/6 inhibitor-based combination with fulves- 12|trant in patients who are treatment na ̈ıve in the advanced setting 13|(ie, patients with de novo disease and those who experienced 14|relapse . 12 months from completion of [neo]adjuvant endocrine 15|therapy with no treatment for advanced disease). Median PFS for this 16|subgroup was not reached for patients receiving ribociclib plus ful- 17|vestrant and was 18.3 months for those in the fulvestrant plus placebo 18|arm, corresponding to a 42% reduction in the risk of progression. 19|Ribociclib plus letrozole also demonstrated improved outcomes in 20|patients who had received no prior therapy in the advanced setting, 21|with a PFS hazard ratio of 0.568, compared with single-agent 22|letrozole.13 These data provide additional confirmation of the use 23|of ribociclib and endocrine therapy combinations, including 24|fulvestrant, as effective first-line treatment for postmenopausal 25|women with HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer. 26|Patients who had received up to one line of prior endocrine 27|therapy for advanced disease also derived benefit from ribociclib 28|plus fulvestrant versus fulvestrant monotherapy, with a median PFS 29|of 14.6 versus 9.1 months, respectively, and a 43% reduction in the 30|risk of progression. In previous phase III studies, CDK4/6 inhibitor 31|and fulvestrant combinations also prolonged PFS versus fulvestrant 32|alone,8,10 confirming the clinical utility of these combinations in 33|patients whose disease progressed during prior endocrine therapy. 34|OS results from MONALEESA-3 were not mature at the time 35|of this analysis. They have yet to be reported for other CDK4/6 36|inhibitors in HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer. 37|Similar to results from other ribociclib studies, ribociclib treat- 38|ment effect was consistent across most prespecified subgroups, further 39|supporting use of ribociclib-based therapy for a broad range of patients 40|with HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer.6,7 Although 41|men were eligible for enrollment after a protocol amendment, no male 42|patients were enrolled. Nevertheless, it remains conceivable that 43|ribociclib plus fulvestrant may also provide benefit in male patients 44|with HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer. 45|The safety profile of ribociclib plus fulvestrant was consistent 46|with that observed in other studies of ribociclib.6,7 Most AEs ob- 47|served in the ribociclib plus fulvestrant arm were of mild or moderate 48|severity, with no new safety signals observed. result.relation_rationale: This is the trial's prespecified primary locally assessed PFS comparison in the randomized population: progression or death from randomization, assessed locally by radiology using RECIST 1.1, comparing ribociclib plus fulvestrant with placebo plus fulvestrant at the first PFS analysis/data cutoff. measurement.method: Local radiology assessment of PFS according to RECIST version 1.1; progression or death from any cause, censoring event-free participants at last adequate tumor assessment.

20|Purpose
21|This phase III study evaluated ribociclib plus fulvestrant in patients with hormone receptor-
22|positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative advanced breast cancer who
23|were treatment na ̈ıve or had received up to one line of prior endocrine therapy in the advanced
24|setting.
25|Patients and Methods
26|Patients were randomly assigned at a two-to-one ratio to ribociclib plus fulvestrant or placebo plus
27|fulvestrant. The primary end point was locally assessed progression-free survival. Secondary end
28|points included overall survival, overall response rate, and safety.
29|Results
30|A total of 484 postmenopausal women were randomly assigned to ribociclib plus fulvestrant, and
31|242 were assigned to placebo plus fulvestrant. Median progression-free survival was significantly
32|improved with ribociclib plus fulvestrant versus placebo plus fulvestrant: 20.5 months (95% CI,
33|18.5 to 23.5 months) versus 12.8 months (95% CI, 10.9 to 16.3 months), respectively (hazard
34|ratio, 0.593; 95% CI, 0.480 to 0.732; P , .001). Consistent treatment effects were observed in
35|patients who were treatment na ̈ıve in the advanced setting (hazard ratio, 0.577; 95% CI, 0.415 to
36|0.802), as well as in patients who had received up to one line of prior endocrine therapy for
37|advanced disease (hazard ratio, 0.565; 95% CI, 0.428 to 0.744). Among patients with measurable
38|disease, the overall response rate was 40.9% for the ribociclib plus fulvestrant arm and 28.7% for
39|placebo plus fulvestrant. Grade 3 adverse events reported in $ 10% of patients in either arm
40|(ribociclib plus fulvestrant v placebo plus fulvestrant) were neutropenia (46.6% v 0%) and leu-
41|kopenia (13.5% v 0%); the only grade 4 event reported in $ 5% of patients was neutropenia
42|(6.8% v 0%).
43|Conclusion
44|Ribociclib plus fulvestrant might represent a new first- or second-line treatment option in hormone
45|receptor-positive/human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-negative advanced breast cancer.

To our knowledge, MONALEESA-3 is the first study 11|to evaluate a CDK4/6 inhibitor-based combination with fulves- 12|trant in patients who are treatment na ̈ıve in the advanced setting 13|(ie, patients with de novo disease and those who experienced 14|relapse . 12 months from completion of [neo]adjuvant endocrine 15|therapy with no treatment for advanced disease). Median PFS for this 16|subgroup was not reached for patients receiving ribociclib plus ful- 17|vestrant and was 18.3 months for those in the fulvestrant plus placebo 18|arm, corresponding to a 42% reduction in the risk of progression. 19|Ribociclib plus letrozole also demonstrated improved outcomes in 20|patients who had received no prior therapy in the advanced setting, 21|with a PFS hazard ratio of 0.568, compared with single-agent 22|letrozole.13 These data provide additional confirmation of the use 23|of ribociclib and endocrine therapy combinations, including 24|fulvestrant, as effective first-line treatment for postmenopausal 25|women with HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer. 26|Patients who had received up to one line of prior endocrine 27|therapy for advanced disease also derived benefit from ribociclib 28|plus fulvestrant versus fulvestrant monotherapy, with a median PFS 29|of 14.6 versus 9.1 months, respectively, and a 43% reduction in the 30|risk of progression. In previous phase III studies, CDK4/6 inhibitor 31|and fulvestrant combinations also prolonged PFS versus fulvestrant 32|alone,8,10 confirming the clinical utility of these combinations in 33|patients whose disease progressed during prior endocrine therapy. 34|OS results from MONALEESA-3 were not mature at the time 35|of this analysis. They have yet to be reported for other CDK4/6 36|inhibitors in HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer. 37|Similar to results from other ribociclib studies, ribociclib treat- 38|ment effect was consistent across most prespecified subgroups, further 39|supporting use of ribociclib-based therapy for a broad range of patients 40|with HR-positive/HER2-negative advanced breast cancer.6,7 Although 41|men were eligible for enrollment after a protocol amendment, no male 42|patients were enrolled. In this phase III, double-blind, placebo-controlled international
study, patients were randomly assigned at a two-to-one ratio to receive
ribociclib (600 mg orally per day; 3 weeks on, 1 week off) plus fulvestrant
(500 mg intramuscularly on day 1 of each 28-day cycle, with an additional
dose on day 15 of cycle 1) or placebo plus fulvestrant. Random assignment
was stratified by the presence or absence of lung or liver metastases (yes v
no) and prior endocrine therapy (treatment na ̈ıve in the advanced setting v
received up to one line of endocrine therapy for advanced disease, as
described in Patients). Treatment continued until disease progression,
unacceptable toxicity, death, or discontinuation for any other reason.

evidence.quote:
Procedures
Tumor response was assessed locally per RECIST (version 1.1) at
screening, every 8 weeks after random assignment for 18 months, and
every 12 weeks thereafter until disease progression, death, withdrawal of
consent, or loss to follow-up; for patients who discontinued for any other
reason, assessments continued per protocol. Imaging data from approx-
imately 40% of randomly selected patients were reviewed centrally by
a blinded independent review committee (BIRC).

Primary End Point
At data cutoff, 210 PFS events had occurred in the ribociclib
plus fulvestrant arm versus 151 in the placebo plus fulvestrant arm.
PFS was significantly improved in the ribociclib plus fulvestrant
arm versus the placebo plus fulvestrant arm, with a median PFS of
20.5 months (95% CI, 18.5 to 23.5 months) versus 12.8 months
(95% CI, 10.9 to 16.3 months), respectively, and a hazard ratio of
0.593 (95% CI, 0.480 to 0.732; P , .001; Fig 2).
PFS analyses based on the BIRC were supportive of the
primary efficacy results. In the 40% of randomly assigned patients
(n = 290) included in the BIRC review, the PFS hazard ratio was
0.492 (95% CI, 0.345 to 0.703).

The captured Source inventory contains only the article and registry projection; no supplement is supplied.

answers.justification: The article reports 210 and 151 PFS events, which are event counts rather than counts of participants with outcome data. The registry's 484 and 242 denominators describe the full analysis set of all randomized participants, not the number observed through progression/death. Follow-up continued after treatment discontinuation unless progression, death, withdrawal, or loss to follow-up occurred, but actual follow-up completeness and censoring counts are not given. Therefore availability for all or nearly all remains unknown.

answers.justification: The article reports a standard time-to-event analysis but no analysis that tests the result under plausible assumptions about missing or censored PFS outcomes. evidence.quote:
Primary and Secondary End Points
The primary end point was locally assessed PFS. To support the primary
end point, a BIRC performed a central assessment of PFS in a randomly selected
subgroup of patients. Secondary end points included overall survival (OS),
overall response rate (ORR), clinical benefit rate, and safety and tolerability.
Statistical Analysis
The primary analysis compared PFS between the treatment arms using
a stratified log-rank test. The treatment effect was estimated using a Cox
proportional hazards model overall and in relevant subgroups. The central PFS
assessment used in support of the primaryefficacyend point was analyzed using
a Cox proportional hazards model. The primary PFS analysis was to be
performed after observing approximately 364 local PFS events to detect a hazard
ratio of 0.67 with 95% power and a one-sided 2.5% level of significance.

Primary End Point
At data cutoff, 210 PFS events had occurred in the ribociclib
plus fulvestrant arm versus 151 in the placebo plus fulvestrant arm.
PFS was significantly improved in the ribociclib plus fulvestrant
arm versus the placebo plus fulvestrant arm, with a median PFS of
20.5 months (95% CI, 18.5 to 23.5 months) versus 12.8 months
(95% CI, 10.9 to 16.3 months), respectively, and a hazard ratio of
0.593 (95% CI, 0.480 to 0.732; P , .001; Fig 2).
PFS analyses based on the BIRC were supportive of the
primary efficacy results. In the 40% of randomly assigned patients
(n = 290) included in the BIRC review, the PFS hazard ratio was
0.492 (95% CI, 0.345 to 0.703).
